title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Routine follow-up for type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient presents for routine follow-up management of their type 2 diabetes. They report feeling well overall and have been adherent with their prescribed medications. They report stable blood glucose levels and no acute changes since the last visit. They deny any signs or symptoms of acute illness.

Medication List
Insulin (specific dosage not provided)
Metformin

Exam
Vitals are stable. Skin exam is unremarkable. Cardiovascular and pulmonary exams are within normal limits. Neurological exam shows intact sensation and motor function. Assessment of overall diabetic status reveals no complications.

Assessment
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with insulin and an oral hypoglycemic agent. The patient has no complications related to their diabetes.

Plan
Continue current regimen of insulin and metformin. Patient to continue monitoring blood glucose as directed. Follow up in three months for routine check and medication reconciliation.
explanations: No complication is documented: type 2 diabetes without complications.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Nothing in the note documents hyperglycemia or poor control.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
